newsitem.title: PANAMA: Strike extended at Panama banana plants.
newsitem.headline: Strike extended at Panama banana plants.

text.p: Striking union workers at banana plantations run by Chiriqui Land Co, Panama's subsidiary of Chiquita Brands International Inc of the United States, strengthened their movement Tuesday after talks with company officials broke down.
"Talks broke down today and are expected to resume tomorrow," assistant Vice President Jorge Solergibert told Reuters.
He said the number of workers involved in the protest had increased to some 3,000 of the total 5,500 employed at Chiriqui plantations on the Atlantic coast.

Workers are protesting proposed lay-offs due to modernization initiatives. The strike began last Wednesday. Chiriqui says the modernizations are needed to meet requirements set by the European Union and make the plantations environmentally-friendly.

The company wants to lay off about 30 percent of the packing station labor force and has offered severance pay. Solergibert said the company was losing about 50,000 18.5-kg boxes in exports each day, or nearly $1.5 million.
Chiriqui accounts for about 85 percent of Panama's banana exports and employs a total 11,000 people.
